column1: # install-set.tsv: every script this repository installs on the box, and where.
# The one list, read by the four places that used to keep their own.
# scripts/deploy.sh routes a changed script to the deploy that installs it,
# scripts/cron-apply.sh schedules it, and scripts/check-hygiene.sh compares the
# installed copy with the checkout. Adding an installed script is one line here.
#   script       the file in scripts/, by name
#   destination  /root/bin, /usr/local/libexec for the member session shell,
#                drain for the directory the drain's own config names
#                at run time (installed into by scripts/deploy-control.sh), or
#                checkout for a script cron runs from the checkout itself, which
#   schedule     the five cron fields, or - when nothing schedules the script
#   args         the arguments the cron line passes, present only when there are
# A script installed in two places has one line per place. lib.sh is sourced by
# the /root/bin scripts and by the drain's, so it is in both. deploy-control.sh
# also installs it beside kyriakon-authcheck in /usr/local/libexec, which has no
# row here because that deploy owns the directory.
# Two scripts are not here, because a row is one file installed under its own
#   - render-docs.sh, which deploy-control.sh runs from the checkout.
# member-git-shell.sh has two rows: the /usr/local/libexec one the login class
# names, and a drain row that puts the source beside provision-member.sh, which
# installs it again when it runs. deploy-mail.sh installs it directly; the drain
# copy is the source the per-member run reads, the way the login class below is.
# Monday, not Sunday. The run creates a box, restores the snapshot into it and
# mails the operator when it fails, and a failure mailed at 03:45 on a Sunday is
# one nobody can act on until Monday anyway: the day is chosen for the morning
# the mail is read, not for the test.
# Read from the checkout rather than installed, so a pull that fixes one is the
# whole change. Both are weekly and an hour apart, so a failure is one mail.
